claims.text: The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is satisfied: the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-02859 and all describe the same journey, the trace running from the 2026-08-15T20:25:06+08:00 trip_started fix to the 2026-08-15T22:43:56+08:00 trip_completed fix, with the fare ledger charged against that same trip.

The measured excess is overwhelming: the trace runs 92.0 km against a booking-time optimal of 22.0 km, an excess of 70.0 km and 318.18% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (excess greater than 0.8 km AND greater than 20%) and both materiality tests pass (excess greater than 8.0 km AND greater than 50%), so the deviation is established and MATERIAL on this trip's own evidence.

The meter time corroborates that the vehicle was driven around rather than merely routed unusually: 138.8 minutes charged against an optimal duration of 30.0 minutes is 108.8 minutes of extra driving on a trip the rider was asleep for, and it lines up with the 92.0 km the trace records.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement, and here it agrees with the trip_record's 92.0 km, so the trace figure is the safe one to use. The trace is also unimpaired for policy purposes: 834 fixes at a 10 second sampling interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 are not met, the trace carries the deviation on its own under POL-RD-08(b), and the escalation trigger in POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

No clause adjusts the comparator route. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 yields no amended optimal and the booked 22.0 km stands as the baseline against which the 92.0 km is measured.

There is no rider instruction anywhere in the record. The chat log for this trip holds zero messages, so there is no rider message, no chat_message.waypoint_hint for POL-RD-04's 200 m corroboration test to run against and no named road; POL-RD-04 is unavailable on this record and no distance is excluded from the excess on account of a rider request.

The driver's only answer, that the rider 'was unresponsive and gave no destination', is a party narrative that cites no evidence ID, names no waypoint and identifies no advisory. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded, and a silent passenger is not the recorded rider instruction that POL-RD-04(a) to (c) requires.

The only traffic advisory artifact in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-02859-01, is admissibility-MISSING, weight 0.0, with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — impaired evidence, disclosed as such — so no advisory covers this corridor in this window, POL-RD-03 cannot be run against anything, and any external traffic cause is weightless under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08. Because no party cites an advisory identifier, this is a gap in the bundle under POL-RD-13(1), not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation.

The rider's profile does not attract the corroboration add-on in POL-RD-08: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, both far below the 4-claim and 1-substantiated thresholds, so no independent corroboration beyond the gps_trace is required — and in any event the excess here is 318.18%, far above the 30% figure that limb names.

The refund is arithmetic, not discretionary. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 22.0 optimal km + 0.28 x 30.0 optimal min) x the 2.0 surge multiplier recorded on the fare_breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee = (28.70 x 2.0) + 0.80 = 58.20. No profile field of either party may ground a finding about this trip: under POL-GEN-01 only the nine (role, field) pairs the policy names are citable, and every other field — rating, account age, trip counts, cancellation rates and the lifetime flag counters — is context only. The 70.0 km excess stands on this trip's own trace, not on anyone's record.

The rider's primary position is the POL-RD-02 figure of SGD 165.95. If the judge treats the SGD 150.00 threshold in POL-RD-10(6) as engaged — the computed refund does exceed it — the consequence under POL-GEN-03 is escalation, with the disputed amount held rather than left collected, which still leaves the rider not carrying the off-route charge. On either path the rider asks only that the 70.0 km they never travelled is not billed to them.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you should know what was found and why no money moves.

WHAT THE RECORD SHOWS. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02859, weight 1.0) ran 92.0 km between the recorded pickup and drop-off. It is complete — 834 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), and its figure agrees with the trip record's 92.0 km. The booking-time optimal route on the trip record (EV-TRIP-02859, weight 1.0) is 22.0 km. The excess is 70.0 km, or 318.18% of optimal: both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (over 0.8 km and over 20%) and both materiality tests (over 8.0 km and over 50%) pass. The deviation is established and MATERIAL on this trip's own evidence. The meter time supports it — 138.8 minutes charged against a 30.0-minute optimal.

NO EXCUSE APPLIES. The chat log (EV-CHAT-02859, weight 1.0) holds zero messages, so there is no rider instruction and no waypoint_hint: POL-RD-04 cannot be run at all, and nothing is excluded from the excess. No pickup or drop-off amendment was recorded (both amendment timestamps and amended_optimal_distance_km are null), so POL-RD-05 yields no amended optimal. The vehicle type is RYDE_X, so the pooled-trip clause POL-RD-12 does not apply. The only traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-02859-01) is admissibility-MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the driver's assertion of an external cause carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13. I record that the assertion was made, that no advisory was on file, and that it does not reduce the excess.

THE ARITHMETIC. The fare is METERED (EV-FARE-02859, weight 1.0). Under POL-RD-02: recomputed_fare = ((SGD 3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 22.0 km + 0.28 x 30.0 min) x the 2.0 surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + SGD 0.80 platform fee = (SGD 28.70 x 2.0) + SGD 0.80 = SGD 58.20. Charged_total is SGD 224.12, so the refund would be SGD 224.12 - SGD 58.20 = SGD 165.92, i.e. SGD 165.95 rounded up. That is 74.03% of charged_total, below the 90% that would make it a full refund, so the rider's recovery on the merits would be a partial refund only. The fare carries no ERP, toll or airport-surcharge lines (0.00, no gantries, trip originates at Jurong Point), so POL-RD-09 adds nothing and nothing is counted twice.

WHY NO MONETARY RULING ISSUES. The refund computed under POL-RD-02, SGD 165.92, exceeds the SGD 150.00 ceiling in POL-RD-10(6). That is a mandatory escalation trigger, and it is the trigger that fired here. Escalation under POL-RD-10 is terminal and replaces the ruling under POL-GEN-03: no refund and no compensation issue, and the disputed amount is held rather than collected or refunded. The rider's own fallback position on this is correct, and the driver's primary position on it is also correct; the two sides simply arrive at the same place from opposite directions.

ON THE REMAINING CLAIMS. The rider's submission that the trace governs under POL-RD-01 is accepted. The rider's point that no profile field may ground a finding about this trip (POL-GEN-01) is accepted and applied. The driver's submission that no POL-RD-06 uplift is available is accepted: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and 0 / 300 completed trips is 0.00, below both thresholds, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and neither the POL-RD-06(a) balance-shift nor the POL-RD-06(b) full-refund uplift is licensed; accordingly no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral fires. The driver's submission that POL-RD-09 adds nothing is accepted; there is no unmatched charge line, so no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral fires either. The rider's claim that the refund would be a partial rather than a full refund is accepted on the figures, but it does not change the outcome, because escalation replaces the monetary ruling altogether.

THE OPEN QUESTION FOR THE REVIEWER, which belongs here rather than in referrals: the computed refund sits just SGD 15.92 above the SGD 150.00 escalation ceiling, and the reviewer should consider whether the ceiling is the right disposition on these figures or whether the optimal route should be re-quoted on a record-type artifact. The reviewer receives the full case summary, both advocates' briefs and the admissibility report. Note also that any monetary effect, had one issued, would have exceeded the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold in POL-GEN-05.

ruling.explanation:
Both sides have run the arithmetic the same way, and I agree with it. The GPS trace for trip TRP-02859 covers the whole journey at a 10-second interval with no gaps, and it records 92.0 km driven — the governing figure under POL-RD-01 — against a booking-time optimal route of 22.0 km. That is an excess of 70.0 km, 318% of optimal, which clears both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (over 20% and over 0.8 km) and both materiality tests (over 50% and over 8.0 km), so the deviation is established AND material. The meter's 138.8 minutes against a 30.0-minute optimal is consistent with the same trace.

Nothing on the record excuses any of it. The chat log for this trip holds zero messages, so there was no rider-requested detour and POL-RD-04 cannot run — no distance is excluded. No pickup or dropoff was amended (both amendment timestamps and amended_optimal_distance_km are null), so POL-RD-05 gives no adjusted comparator. This is a metered RYDE_X trip, not pooled and not upfront-quoted, so POL-RD-11 and POL-RD-12 do not apply. The only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-02859-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0, so no closure can be shown and POL-RD-03 is unavailable (POL-RD-13). The driver's statement that the rider 'was unresponsive and gave no destination' cites no evidence ID, names no waypoint and identifies no advisory; under POL-RD-08 it carries no weight, and POL-RD-14 does not apply because there was no instruction for the trace to corroborate.

The refund is then arithmetic under POL-RD-02: (base fare 3.80 + 0.75 x 22.0 km + 0.28 x 30.0 min) x the 2.0 surge multiplier read from the fare breakdown = 28.70 x 2.0 = 57.40, plus the 0.80 platform fee = a recomputed fare of 58.20. The charged total was 224.12, so the refund is 224.12 - 58.20 = 165.92, which rounds up to 165.95. It is 74.0% of the charge, below the 90% share that would convert it to a full refund, so on its own it would be a partial refund. No ERP, toll or surcharge line is added on top, because the fare carries none and the trip did not originate at an airport (POL-RD-09).

That refund of 165.92 exceeds the SGD 150.00 ceiling in POL-RD-10(6). That trigger is mandatory and terminal under POL-GEN-03: I cannot issue the money myself. The case goes to a human reviewer with the full file, no money moves, and the disputed amount is held rather than refunded. The reviewer's question is whether to release the POL-RD-02 refund of 165.95 or vary it; the record is otherwise complete and no further evidence is needed. No referral is made: the driver's POL-RD-06 check is clean (deviation_flags_90d of 0 over completed_trips_90d of 300, so no pattern is established), and there is no phantom billing line to refer under POL-RD-09(4). The rider's profile likewise attracts no corroboration add-on under POL-RD-08. Confidence is 0.95, drawn from the fare breakdown, trip record and GPS trace, all at full weight and none impaired.

Both of you should see where this lands and why. The measurement is not in dispute. For trip TRP-02859 the GPS trace runs 92.0 km against a booking-time optimal route of 22.0 km — an excess of 70.0 km, or 318.18% of optimal — so under POL-RD-01 the deviation is ESTABLISHED and MATERIAL, and the trace that carries it is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 (834 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s), so nothing about a broken trace changes the picture and the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is met. No clause excuses the excess: the chat log holds zero messages, so there is no rider-requested detour for POL-RD-04 to act on; pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, so POL-RD-05 changes no comparator; and the only traffic advisory in the bundle (EV-ADVIS-02859-01) is admissibility-MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and any 'traffic was bad' explanation carries no weight under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08. The driver's statement that the rider was unresponsive cites no evidence ID and does not satisfy POL-RD-04(a)–(c). The POL-RD-06 check on the driver comes back clean — deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 300 — so no pattern is established and neither the uplift nor a conduct referral follows.

On the arithmetic the rider asked for: the fare is METERED and the surge multiplier of 2.0 is read from the fare_breakdown (not the trip_record). POL-RD-02 gives recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 × 22.0 + 0.28 × 30.0) × 2.0) + 0.80 = (28.70 × 2.0) + 0.80 = 58.20. Charged_total is 224.12, so the refund would be 224.12 − 58.20 = 165.92, rounded up to SGD 165.95. That is 74.03% of charged_total, below the 90% share that would convert it to a full refund, and there are no ERP or surcharge lines for POL-RD-09 to add on top.

That refund figure is why no money moves today. POL-RD-10(6) makes a computed POL-RD-02 refund above SGD 150.00 a mandatory escalation, and 165.92 exceeds it. I am therefore not permitted to issue the monetary ruling either side's arithmetic points to: the ruling is ESCALATE, it is terminal and it replaces any money outcome, and the SGD 116.50 in dispute is held rather than collected or refunded. No clause produces a referral here (POL-RD-06(c) does not fire, and there is no POL-RD-09(4) phantom or misapplied line), so the referrals list is empty. The human reviewer receives the deviation finding, the 165.92 computation and the missing advisory. The open question for that reviewer, which belongs here rather than in a referral, is whether the escalation ceiling is meant to catch a refund of this size or whether the comparator route should be adjusted — nothing on this record adjusts it, and no advisory, chat instruction or amendment is available to do so.
